Fixture: 61_vardct_gradient_128x128_nofilters_d1.jxl
128x128 RGB gradient, VarDCT d1.0, filters off --
OPEN BUG REPRODUCER: the minimal stream that trips G.2.2 LfQuant's C.3.2 check

Purpose
-------
The 644-byte minimisation of fixtures 54 and 57, whose G.2.2 `LfQuant`
modular sub-bitstream fails its own C.3.2 terminal-state check and so blocks
VarDCT acceptance. Two things were shrunk away:

  * **Content.** 54/57's source is half smooth gradient, half 1-pixel
    magenta/cyan checkerboard. The checkerboard is irrelevant: a pure
    128x128 gradient fails identically, and a pure 128x128 checkerboard
    decodes fine. So the trigger is smooth content, not high frequency.
  * **Size.** Encoding the same gradient at 16, 32, 48, 64, 72, 80, 88, 96,
    104 and 112 all decode; 120, 128 and 136 all fail. The transition sits
    between 112 and 120, i.e. between LfQuant channels of 14x14 and 15x15.
    Non-square variants (128x64, 64x128, 128x16, 16x128) all decode, so
    BOTH dimensions have to be past the threshold.

That transition is the most useful fact in this fixture: it says the trigger
is a property of the LF channel's size, not of the image content, and it
gives a 644-byte stream (vs 2316 for fixture 54) to trace by hand.

The failing sub-bitstream's MA tree is
`property[1] > 2 ? West : (property[15] > 0 ? ... : ...)` with both
non-`West` leaves `SelfCorrecting` -- property 1 is the stream index and
property 15 is `max_error`, so this is the same H.5 weighted-predictor
surface as the sawtooth fixture 60. See
docs/experiments/2026-08-03-h52-clamp-lower-gate-and-sawtooth.md.

Verification
------------
This fixture is LOSSY, so there is no byte-identical round-trip to check.
tools/make-debug-fixtures.sh verifies only that djxl accepts the stream and
reports 128x128 -- enough to establish that the stream is conformant and the
failure is JPXL's.

cjxl is used strictly as a BLACK BOX: it emits conformant streams for JPXL to
parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a different libjxl
revision changes these digests, that is the point of recording them -- do not
silently update them; note the revision change.
